titles.title: UnrealGold
titles.engine: Unreal Engine 1: Unreal Gold 226b (Manifest.ini Version=226b; Unreal plus Return to Na Pali/UPak). The game renderer is D3DDrv 226b (System\D3DDrv.dll, md5 f924e209e7bc23b90b6f0360174683d3), a DirectX 7 renderer (IDirectDraw7 plus IID_IDirect3D7). The menus are UWindow/UMenu. Unreal.ini sets Console=UPak.UPakConsole. UPak.u's import table resolves its superclass to UMenu.UnrealConsole, which extends UWindow.WindowConsole.
titles.launch_sets: CONFIRMED: the game starts fullscreen at 1920x1080x32 on all four LCD boxes. 'Play Unreal Gold.bat' calls FLEETRES.BAT, then FLEETRES.EXE -ini writes FullscreenViewportX/Y=%FR_W%/%FR_H% and StartupFullscreen=True, and sets Game/Windowed/RenderDevice to %FR_UE1DEV%. gameres.h lines 721-723 write the same three WinDrv keys at GAMESYNC time, but not the render device. At about 00:45 I ran FLEETRES.EXE -cmd (read-only) on each box. It printed FR_W=1920, FR_H=1080, FR_EDID=1, FR_GLIDE=0 and FR_UE1DEV=D3DDrv.D3DRenderDevice on .123, .145, .195 and .240; .240's EDID was present at that time. The deployed Unreal.ini already reads 1920/1080 on all four boxes. SetRes chooses the mode by searching the full DirectDraw list, not the capped GetRes list. Proof: .195's Unreal.log from 08-31 reads 'Best-match display mode: 1920x1080x32 (Error=0)', although 1080p is only the 20th 16-bpp mode on that box. .145 had never been tested at 1080p; tonight it started at 1920x1080x32 (same best-match line in Unreal.log, and a 1920x1080 frame).
titles.menu_source: The list comes from the driver and is cut short. Esc opens the UWindow desktop (UMenuRootWindow); the path is Options > Preferences > Video > Resolution. UMenuVideoClientWindow.LoadAvailableSettings copies ConsoleCommand("GetRes") word for word into a combo that cannot be typed into. The renderer's Exec runs before WinDrv's, so D3DDrv answers GetRes. It keeps each distinct WxH among the 16-bpp entries of IDirectDraw7::EnumDisplayModes, in DirectDraw's order and unsorted, and prints only the first 16 (100064f5: cmp edi,0x10). The only other filter is a max-size clamp, which is 0x7fffffff except on a 3dfx Voodoo 1 or 2. I measured the lists tonight with a probe that makes the same EnumDisplayModes call (flags 0, DDSD_CAPS/DDSCAPS_3DDEVICE). The distinct 16-bpp modes are in ascending order on every box. .123 has 15, and 1920x1080 is 15th, so it is listed. .145 has 16, and 1920x1080 is 16th, so it is listed with no margin. .195 has 20, and 1920x1080 is 20th, so it is cut and the menu stops at 1440x900. .240 has 24, and 1920x1080 is 24th, so it is cut; the menu runs from 320x200 to 1280x768. Observed in-game on .145: getres printed exactly the 16 predicted modes, ending in 1920x1080. Result: the menu lists 1920x1080 on .123 and .145, but not on .195 or .240.

titles.fix:
CONFIRMED as proposed: edit one byte of System\D3DDrv.dll at file offset 0x64f5, changing 83 FF 10 (cmp edi,16) to 83 FF 7F. After the edit, D3DDrv prints every distinct 16-bpp mode in DirectDraw's order, which is ascending on all four LCD boxes. UMenu's combo has no item limit, so the menu should show 20 entries ending at 1920x1080 on .195 and 24 entries ending at 1920x1080 on .240; these are the probe's full lists. GameRenderDevice stays D3DDrv, as README-FLEET requires. Ship it through the staged-game loop:
1. Back up the original under Games-Library\_patches and record both md5s in _patches\README.txt.
2. Publish through gvfs. The edit keeps the file size, and smbclient stamps an Oct 2007 mtime that makes GAMESYNC skip the file.
3. On every box run GAMESYNC RESET, then GAMESYNC START. The boot-time sync stays idle while gamesync.done exists.
4. DOWNLOAD the DLL from each box and compare its md5.
The survey's rejected alternatives are still worse. The 226 OpenGlDrv (verified sorted and uncapped) contradicts README-FLEET, and FR_UE1DEV would overwrite an ini-only switch anyway. OldUnreal 227 needs SSE2 and cannot join a 226 server.
titles.fix_source: No payload is needed; it is an edit of the staged file. The 226 Final patch on the share (Game Updates\unreal-patch-226-final.exe) embeds a D3DDrv.dll at offset 0x11cdced, md5 7984caa1280d74fcb6c32bfa9d1522cb. I re-carved it: it has the same 83 FF 10 at 0x64f5, so applying the patch does not help. A case-insensitive search of Files\ and Utility\ found no other Unreal 226 renderer. The utglr 3.6 and utd3d9r 1.3 files in Utility\Retro Automation are UT 436 renderers and cannot load in 226.
titles.fix_risk: Low. D3DDrv.dll is a client renderer, not a network package, so the UCC LAN host and 226 multiplayer are unaffected. GetRes builds its output in a string device that grows as needed, and UMenu parses any number of entries. One side effect: the classic UnrealShare.UnrealVideoMenu (var string Resolutions[16]) would log 'Accessed array out of bounds' if it were opened with more than 16 modes, because UnrealScript clamps that write. That menu is not on the Esc path here, which is the UMenu console, so this is harmless. The general cautions for a same-size vendor-binary edit still apply: keep the md5s, publish through gvfs, and verify on each box.
titles.hw_check:
This procedure was validated tonight on .145 while it was idle.
1. Check first that no other session is running a game on the box (PROCLIST/WINLIST).
2. Start the game: EXEC cmd /c start "" /D "C:\Games\UnrealGold" "Play Unreal Gold.bat". Wait about 40 s.
3. UIKEY TILDE opens the 'System Console'. Press it ONCE only: a second TILDE closes the console, so type any later command without it.
4. UIKEY TEXT:getres, then UIKEY ENTER.
5. SCREENSHOT 0. GDI captured the D3D fullscreen frame on XP. The console prints one mode per line; the menu receives the same modes as one space-separated string.
6. Pass: 1920x1080 appears on .123, .145, .195 and .240. Expected today: present on .123 and .145 (seen on .145); absent on .195, whose last line is 1440x900, and on .240, whose last line is 1280x768. After the fix it should be present on all four.
7. Clean up: EXEC taskkill /f /im "Unreal.exe", then DISPLAYCFG get should read 1920x1080x32. No Running.ini was left behind.
The Video drop-down itself uses a relative-mouse cursor, so a person has to open it.
titles.verifier_notes: Confirmed, and the survey's unproven parts are now measured. (1) I re-disassembled D3DDrv independently. Confirmed: the 16-bpp filter, dedup with no sort, cap bytes 83 FF 10 at 0x64f5, the 0x7fffffff clamp (set at 0x10001d88, lowered only for VEN_121A dev 1/2), and IDirectDraw7 EnumDisplayModes with flags 0. (2) The survey's per-box counts were GDI-based predictions. The DirectDraw probe now measures them: 15, 16, 20 and 24, as predicted. On .145 the raw DirectDraw order is grouped by depth, but the distinct 16-bpp list is still ascending. (3) The in-game getres on .145 matches the probe's emulation line for line, which validates the .195 and .240 results. (4) .145 is now proven at 1080p launch. My .145 run changed the box's Unreal.ini the same way any play session does. The launcher set WindowedRenderDevice=D3DDrv. The engine rewrote LocalMap, SkinDetail and TextureDetail. The diff is saved. (5) Added the GAMESYNC RESET/START deployment steps and the classic-menu note.

titles.title: UnrealTournament
titles.engine: Unreal Engine 1: UT99 OldUnreal 469e ([FirstRun] 469; Manifest.ini still says 436). GameRenderDevice=D3D9Drv.D3D9RenderDevice, 469e's own Direct3D 9 renderer, md5 01bb5c61f3f1c4744ea34f8072141cbc. The build needs SSE2 and its PE files are XP-only.
titles.launch_sets: CONFIRMED: fullscreen 1920x1080x32. 'Play Unreal Tournament.bat' writes FullscreenViewportX/Y=%FR_W%/%FR_H% and StartupFullscreen=True into System\UnrealTournament.ini, and gameres.h lines 724-726 write the same keys. FLEETRES -cmd printed 1920/1080 on all four LCD boxes. The deployed UnrealTournament.ini on all four reads 1920/1080x32 with D3D9Drv. The compat DB records 1920x1080 frames on .123, .240 and .246 (now .195). Tonight on .145, which had not been tested before, 469e also filled a 1920x1080 frame with its intro (145-ut469e-getres/02b-after-getcurrentres.png).
titles.menu_source: The full list, taken from the driver: not a table and not filtered by aspect. The path is Options > Preferences > Video > Resolution. 469e's UMenuVideoClientWindow first reads GetScreenMode to fill its new window-mode combo, then copies GetRes word for word into a combo that cannot be typed into. 469e's WinDrv viewport Exec has two GetRes branches. In fullscreen, D3D9Drv answers with every mode at the viewport depth (32), minus 320x200 and 640x400, de-duplicated, sorted with appQsort, and with no cap. Windowed or borderless, WinDrv filters the renderer's list and a built-in table to the desktop size; the table is at file 0x31af8 and includes 1920x1080. On a 1080p desktop, both paths list 1920x1080.

GameRenderDevice=OpenGLDrv.OpenGLRenderDevice (retail 436 OpenGlDrv.dll, md5 12031672ff432601cf638efe2e26acd6) with FullscreenColorBits=16. requires.json excludes nothing, so it is deployed on .123, .145, .195 and .240 as well as the pre-SSE2 boxes.

The emulated 436 GetRes at 16 bpp ends in 1920x1080 on every box: 15 entries on .123, 16 on .145, 20 on .195, 22 on .240. Caveat: if a player uses the Video page's driver button to switch to this tree's D3DDrv.dll, that renderer has the same 16-bpp-only, 16-entry cap as Unreal Gold's.

titles.title: UT2004
titles.engine: Unreal Engine 2: UT2004 ECE build 3369 (System\Build.ini UT2004_Build_[2005-11-23_16.22]). RenderDevice=D3DDrv.D3DRenderDevice (Direct3D 8). The menus are GUI2K4 (UT2K4GUIController), with XInterface.ExtendedConsole as the console.
titles.launch_sets: CONFIRMED: 1920x1080 fullscreen. 'Play UT2004.bat' and 'Join fleet UT2004 server.bat' both write FullscreenViewportX/Y and StartupFullscreen into System\UT2004.ini, and gameres.h lines 730-732 write the same keys. The deployed UT2004.ini reads 1920/1080 on all four LCD boxes. The compat DB shows 1920x1080 on .123, .240 and .246 (now .195). .145 has not been tested.
titles.menu_source: A hardcoded table plus the current mode. The path is Settings > Display (UT2K4Tab_DetailSettings). I decoded it independently. DisplayModes[17] is 320x240, 512x384, 640x480, 800x500, 800x600, 1024x640, 1024x768, 1152x768, 1152x864, 1280x800, 1280x854, 1280x960, 1280x1024, 1600x1024, 1600x1200, 1680x1050, 1920x1200: no 1920x1080. It is not a config variable, and the co_Resolution combo has bReadOnly=True. CheckSupportedResolutions removes table entries that SUPPORTEDRESOLUTION rejects and re-adds supported ones, but never clears the list. InternalOnLoadINI inserts GetCurrentRes in sorted order through AddNewResolution. CORRECTION: the page IS persistent. UT2k4MainPage's defaults set bPersistent=True and bRestorable=True (tag bytes d3 at 0x2e369 and 0x2e36d), and UT2K4SettingsPage inherits them. When Settings is reopened, GUIController.CreateMenu reuses the same page object from PersistentStack. PushMenu calls InitComponent only when Controller==None, and GUIPage.Free() does nothing for a persistent page. So the list built at the first open (the table plus 1920x1080) survives closing and reopening, level changes, and a switch to another mode. It lacks 1920x1080 only when Settings is first opened in a session that did not start at 1080p, and neither staged launcher starts one that way.

titles.title: DeusEx
titles.engine: Unreal Engine 1: Deus Ex 1112fm (SYSTEM\MANIFEST.INI Version=1112fm). GameRenderDevice is Deus Ex's own D3DDrv (SYSTEM\D3DDRV.DLL, md5 6179c83ce1d7516908e5442ebfb4d154). The launchers do not write the render device. The UI is Deus Ex's own (DeusEx.DeusExRootWindow, extension window system).
titles.launch_sets: CONFIRMED: fullscreen 1920x1080x32. 'Play Deus Ex.bat' and 'Host Deus Ex Multiplayer.bat' write FullscreenViewportX/Y and StartupFullscreen into SYSTEM\DeusEx.ini, and gameres.h lines 733-735 write the same keys. The deployed DeusEx.ini on all four LCD boxes reads 1920x1080x32 with D3DDrv. SetRes searches the full DirectDraw list: .195's DeusEx.log from 08-31 reads 'Best-match display mode: 1920x1080x32 (Error=0)', although 1080p is not in that box's capped menu list. .123 is verified at 1920x1080. .240 runs, but GDI returns black there. .145 has not been tested.
titles.menu_source: The list comes from the driver and is cut short twice. The path is Settings (4th main-menu button) > Display (4th) > Resolution, which is MenuChoice_Resolution. GetScreenResolutions parses GetRes, keeping at most 16 tokens (the loop is bounded by ArrayCount of an unused Resolutions[16] local) and dropping widths under 640. GetRes comes from D3DDRV.DLL, which has the same algorithm as Unreal Gold's: 16 bpp only, unsorted, at most 16 entries (100062ce cmp edi,0x10). I measured the resulting menus with the probe. On .123, 15 entries include 1920x1080. On .145, 16 entries end in 1920x1080; the identical algorithm was confirmed in-game with Unreal Gold on that box. On .195 the menu has 16 entries, 640x480 to 1440x900. On .240 it has 12 entries, 640x400 to 1280x768. TRAP, worse than the survey said: if the current mode is not in the list, LoadSetting selects entry 0. MenuUIWindow defaults bEscapeSavesSettings=True and the Display screen inherits it, so Esc runs SaveSettings exactly as Enter and OK do. That calls SetRes on entry 0: 640x480 on .195, 640x400 on .240. Today, simply opening Display Settings and leaving with Esc drops those boxes out of 1080p.

titles.fix:
CONFIRMED: two one-byte edits, and both are required.
(1) SYSTEM\D3DDRV.DLL at 0x62ce: change 83 FF 10 to 83 FF 7F.
(2) SYSTEM\DEUSEX.U at 0x4607ce: change 0x10 to 0x28.
Checks on (2): it is the only IntConstByte 16 in GetScreenResolutions. The Resolutions[16] local is never referenced in the bytecode, and writes go to enumText[choiceCount] with choiceCount at most 39, which is within enumText[40]. Expected menus after both edits: on .195, 20 entries ending in 1920x1080; on .240, 20 entries (640x400 up to 1920x1080). LoadSetting then selects 1920x1080, so neither Esc nor OK issues a SetRes; the trap goes away too. Deploy the same way as Unreal Gold:
1. Back up the originals and record their md5s in _patches\README.txt.
2. Publish through gvfs.
3. Run GAMESYNC RESET, then GAMESYNC START, on every box.
4. Verify both bytes on each box by DOWNLOAD and md5.
titles.fix_source: No payload is needed: both are edits of staged files. The share has no Deus Ex SDK or UCC; a case-insensitive search found none. The _patches\backup-2026-08-29-deusex-1112fm copies are the pre-1112fm files. Kentie's Deus Exe is not on the share, and I did not re-check its web changelog.
titles.fix_risk: Moderate. DEUSEX.U is a network package, but the edit keeps its GUID and size, so saves and the package map still match. I looked for a content check and found none. The login URL's Checksum= option is the ngStats one: Engine.dll sends 'Checksum=NoChecksum' when no stats password is set, which is what the .145 server log shows, and GameInfo only logs it. Still re-prove a join to the fleet 1112fm server and a box-hosted LAN game after deploying. Both files keep their size, so publish through gvfs. Until the fix ships, warn players on .195 and .240 not to open Display Settings.
titles.hw_check:
1. Check PROCLIST/WINLIST first.
2. EXEC cmd /c start "" /D "C:\Games\DeusEx" "Play Deus Ex.bat"
3. The menu cursor uses relative mouse movement, so UICLICK misses. On the screens, Left/Right cycle the focused choice, and buttons carry |& accelerators (Cancel is |&C); whether a bare letter fires an accelerator is unverified.
4. Capture with SCREENSHOT 0, or with Ctrl+F9 (UIKEY CTRL+F9), which DeusExRootWindow hard-codes to SHOT and which works inside menus; then DOWNLOAD SYSTEM\Shot####.bmp. Use Ctrl+F9 on .240, where GDI is black.
5. Leave only with the Cancel button or taskkill /f /im "DeusEx.exe". NEVER press Esc, Enter or OK there before the fix: all three save the settings.
6. Proxy with no Deus Ex menu at all: Unreal Gold's console getres on the same box runs the identical D3DDrv algorithm (validated on .145). Take its first 16 tokens and keep those at least 640 wide.
titles.verifier_notes: The 'no' and the fix are confirmed. I verified the bytes, the export offsets, and that the edit cannot write out of bounds. The .195 and .240 menus are now measured rather than predicted. CORRECTED: the survey's hw_check said to 'Leave the screen with Escape (Cancel), never Enter/OK'. That is wrong: MenuUIWindow.bEscapeSavesSettings defaults True and only Load Game and New Game turn it off, so Esc also applies entry 0. On .240, entry 0 is 640x400, not 640x480. ADDED: the ngStats-only login checksum finding, Ctrl+F9 as a way to capture inside menus, and the GAMESYNC RESET/START deployment step.
